newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATHLETICS-GREENE AND TIEDTKE COMPLETE FAMILY DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GREENE AND TIEDTKE COMPLETE FAMILY DOUBLE.

text.p: American Joe Greene and his German wife Susan Tiedtke completed a family double with respective victories in the long jump competitions at Pretoria's Pilditch Stadium on Wednesday.

Greene, the current world indoor bronze medallist, recorded an impressive jump of 8.30 metres in the second Engen Grand Prix summer series meeting -- a five-centimetre improvement on his winning effort in Pietersburg last week.
Tiedtke, a former double world indoor medallist, took the women's honours with a leap of 6.76 metres.

Namibia's double Olympic silver medallist Frankie Fredericks was expected to produce something special in the 200 metres, particularly after his wind-assisted 9.99 seconds in the 100 metres a week ago.
But Fredericks, although victorious, disappointed with his winning time of 20.20 seconds in a meeting held at 1,400 metres above sea level.
Olympic discus champion Lars Riedel of Germany won his discipline with a throw of 64.56 metres, with fellow-countryman Michael Mollenbeck next best with 63.34 metres.
Of the South African performances on Wednesday, Olympic silver medallist Hezekiel Sepeng was the most impressive in winning the 800 metres in a world-class time of one minute 45.56 seconds.
Llewellyn Herbert equalled the South African senior record he set last week in the 400 metres hurdles with a winning performance of 48.35 seconds.

In the pole vault, Pretoria-based Riaan Botha overshadowed All-African record-holder Okkert Brits with a career-best 5.91 metres. Botha pushed his fellow-South African into second place on 5.86 metres.
